anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
A fits better because the current code already has a single settings path for this view. `settings/resolver.ts:12` owns the defaults, and the traced data path shows those resolved values reaching `ui/report-view.ts:30`. A new key in the resolver uses the same defaults, resolution, and consumption path as every existing setting. A view-local settings object would add a second settings path beside the resolver. Its defaults could drift from the resolver's, and the view would then read from two sources. So the design will add the setting as a resolver key that the report view reads through its existing resolved settings.

Next is the behavior the setting controls. When the user switches workspaces, what should happen to the report filters that are currently active?
A) a resolver setting chooses the behavior and defaults to resetting filters on a workspace change
B) a resolver setting chooses the behavior and defaults to keeping filters, which matches today's behavior
C) filters always reset on a workspace change, so no user-facing choice is needed
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - resetting by default stops filters from silently hiding rows in the new workspace, and the setting still lets users keep their filters across workspaces.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Reusing the resolver fits because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. The new setting can follow that same path without introducing a separate view-local source of truth.

What should the new setting do when the workspace changes?
A) Reset report filters when enabled; preserve today’s behavior when disabled.
B) Remember filters separately for each workspace and restore them on return.
C) Keep filters active, but make their effect more visible rather than resetting them.
D) other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it directly addresses hidden rows while reusing the existing settings path and avoiding per-workspace filter storage.
